nodes.label: lockup.svg (Steigenberger brand lockup)
nodes.rationale: The brand lockup used over the hero on the auth screens: a hand-flattened 144x53 SVG, three orders of magnitude smaller than the card artwork (14 KB vs ~700 KB-1.2 MB). One embedded PNG for the STEIGENBERGER wordmark plus 19 outlined paths for the two property lines. Drawn at its natural size and never scaled, so its glyphs land within ~1px of where the 390px design board places them.

nodes.label: Frame 1.svg (lockup design export)
nodes.rationale: The upstream design export the shipped lockup is derived from, named explicitly in lockup.svg's own header comment. It draws STEIGENBERGER as two overlaid 486x242 PNGs (artwork plus a separate luminance mask), which is why it could not be dropped in unmodified. Lives alongside the card exports in the svg files/ directory.

nodes.label: Flattened Wordmark Composite
nodes.source_location: header comment + single <image x=2.6795 y=3.2995 width=137.6259 height=13.2027>
nodes.rationale: Stated verbatim in the file's own comment: the export draws STEIGENBERGER as two overlaid 486x242 PNGs — artwork plus a separate luminance mask — so any engine that does not composite the pair renders an opaque rectangle instead of a wordmark. The two are therefore composited once, ahead of time, into a single transparent image placed at the rect they shared, and the HOTEL & RESIDENCE and DOHA paths are carried over from the export unaltered. Rendered on top of each other, the export and the flattened asset are the same picture.

nodes.label: Steigenberger Wordmark Stack
nodes.source_location: image y=3.3 + '<!-- HOTEL & RESIDENCE -->' paths + '<!-- DOHA -->' paths
nodes.rationale: A three-tier mark, explicitly sectioned by comments in the file: the STEIGENBERGER raster wordmark on top; HOTEL & RESIDENCE beneath it as silver #C0C5C7 outlined glyphs at y approx 21-30; and DOHA below that, centred, in cream #EDEAE4 at y approx 41-48. The artwork is what settles the property's full name as 'Steigenberger Hotel & Residence Doha' — two lines, two sizes, two colours — a distinction that collapses whenever the mark is attempted as live text.
